BiblicalUsage: heptá — seven. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 62 occurrences, and in Matthew, Mark, Luke, and Acts the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: What heptá tells me is that seven is the Bible’s number of completeness — God finished His work and rested. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
RelatedEvents: The Feeding of the Four Thousand; The Presentation of Jesus in the Temple; The Appointment of the Seven
